title: Dungeon Builder: The Demon King’s Labyrinth is a Modern City!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a world where demon lords build dungeons and feed on human fear and despair, rookie demon lord Procel wants instead to build a dungeon where humans and monsters live together happily, a 'modern city'. With his mentor Marcho and created minions, he must first defeat a rival, the Wind Demon Lord. Seven Seas markets the adaptation of the light novels as a 'sexy fantasy tale'.
life_message: Building a prosperous community where different peoples can live together beats ruling through fear.

content.note: Battles between demon lords with guns and magic (AniList Guns, Magic); MU Violence and Blood and Gore.
Dungeons harvesting fear and despair (Manga Bookshelf).
Ecchi genre (AniList, MU), Nudity (AniList, MU), Sexual Innuendo; 'plenty' of fan service and youthful-looking minions joked about (Manga Bookshelf); MU Sexual Assault (context to verify).
Crude jokes noted ('Lolicel' nickname per Manga Bookshelf).
Guns used casually in fantasy combat (AniList Guns).
Economics and city-building are the premise (AniList Economics, Kingdom Management).

dominant: Coexistence and city-building; demon lord rivalry; fan service

frames.aligns: Procel's goal of a peaceful city where humans and monsters coexist echoes the common good.
frames.concerns: Heavy fan service and nudity, sexualized youthful-looking minions, demon-lord protagonist.
Passions inflamed by sexual imagery; demonic hero.

frames.aligns: Choosing a peaceful dungeon over terror.
frames.concerns: Ecchi content and demon lords presented heroically.
Demon lords, summoning and sexual imagery.

frames.aligns: Welcoming outsiders into a shared city.
frames.concerns: Content does not tend to holiness.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Rival demon lords settle disputes by battle; Procel seeks prosperity instead of terror.

Order vs freedom.evidence: A planned city run by its demon lord.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyal created minions; a city open to humans and monsters.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Demon lord over his created monsters (MU Dungeon Master, Summoned Creatures).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern city planning and economics replace traditional dungeons (AniList Economics).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival against rival demon lords alongside comfort-seeking.

folkways.japan: Light-novel kingdom-building and harem conventions, including youthful-looking characters, shape the series in ways typical of the Japanese isekai market.

delivery.evidence: Manga Bookshelf finds no clear message; the coexistence goal is only sketched in volume 1.

personified.ideology: traditional demon lord rule through fear

delivery.note: The coexistence idea is the premise rather than an argued message; the rival demon lord represents the old way.

winners_losers: Procel's coexistence city is set up to win; demon lords who rule by fear are rivals.
